name: 'Tomorrow is Built Today' exhibition of Black-led self-build
description: Open House of 13 Nubia Way  and oral history exhibition of Europe's largest black-led community self-build for rent initiative including archive material and new video. https://sites.gold.ac.uk/inlivingmemory/tomorrow-is-built-today/

name: 1 Halliwick Road
description: A low energy refurbishment of an Edwardian house, with rear extension and loft conversion. Wood fibre insulation, MVHR, airtightness layer, triple glazing, timber structure and low embodied energy materials.

name: 1 Pontypool Place
description: Tour of home & garden designed in 2018 by Nagan Johnson Architects
address: 1 Pontypool Place London London, Greater London, SE1 8QF

name: 1 Waterlow Court
description: Grade II* listed Arts and Crafts gem  designed by Baillie-Scott
address: Flat 1 Waterlow Court, Heath Close, NW11 7DT

name: 141 Coldershaw Road, W13
description: The home of Eric and Jessica Huntley , community activists and educators who founded the pioneering company Bogle-L'Ouverture Publications in 1968, lived and ran their bookshop from this semi detached property soon after.  The house is a Black British cultural archivists dream; filled with books, arts and craft and correspondence from the 1960s to the present day.

name: 195 Mare Street
description: 195 Mare Street

name: 2 Belgrave Road: Victorian house with Luis Barragán inspired interior
description:
A Luis Barragán inspired design for the interior of a typical late Victorian house in East London. 
The use of bold vivid colour banishes the sterility that can accompany modernism without the loss of its hallmark simplicity and elegant line. This approach can be accommodated within houses whose external architecture has a very different heritage. Its achievement does not require a big budget

name: 7 Meadow Lane
description: Open House of 7 Meadow Lane, Charmaine McNally’s home and garden. Charmaine was one of the self-build leaders in this 14 home women-led community self-build scheme.  Meadow Lane was originally the third of  Fusion Jameen’s schemes. Tim Oshodi was engaged as self-build consultant, with project management and cost control provided by Survey Design Partnership and Martin Hughes, the contracts manager

name: 81 Columbia Road
description: Step into the historic charm of 81 Columbia Road Flower Market in East London.  This iconic Victorian terraced house functions as a space for a local artist who has focussed on photographs of London architecture and life.

name: A House for Artists
description: A House for Artists (AHFA) is an experiment in communal living and working, that seeks to embed artists very directly into the local community in a meaningful way. The model combines 12 rented flats, occupied by artists and their families/flatmates, with a ground floor community/work space. Each artist in the house volunteers their time to shape different strands of a growing public programme.

name: ACAVA Camden Undercraft Studios
description:
ACAVA Undercraft Studios
A vital creative hub in Gospel Oak, home to 34 fully accessible artist studios and 10 community organisations.
address: Blue Double Door, 48-72 Ludham, Lismore Circus,, NW5 4SF

name: Aga Khan Centre
description: The Aga Khan Centre, designed by Pritzker prize winning architect Fumihiko Maki, houses the UK institutions of the Aga Khan Development Network. A unique feature is its six gardens inspired by different regions of the Muslim world.
address: Aga Khan Centre, 10 Handyside Street, N1C 4DN

name: Art in Perpetuity Trust
description: Open Studios, provides a unique glimpse to the architectural spaces and working studios of APT artists.  Over the weekend, there is also the opportunity to see our Group Show in the Gallery, curated by and featuring APT artist's work.

name: Artist Niamh Hannaford at One North Quay Canary Wharf
description: Set within the construction site of One North Quay, Canary Wharf, join us for a performance and installation presented by artist Niamh Hannaford using materials donated from the Canary Wharf construction site. This is an opportunity to gain exclusive access to a monumental building currently under construction, which will eventually house companies on the cutting edge of science and innovation.
address: One North Quay, Canary Wharf, E14 5GJ

name: BT Tower
description: An enduring, distinctive feature of the London skyline for the last 54 years, this is a rare opportunity for members of the public to visit the famous revolving floor, 158m above the capital. After the flight the guests can watch a history of the BT Tower film in our auditorium.

name: Bank of England Museum
description: The museum is part of the Bank of England rebuilding in the 1930's by Sir Herbert Baker. One room is a reconstruction of 1793 Bank of England Stock Office by Sir John Soane.

name: Bodney Road Studios
description: Bodney Road Studio's is home to a range of practitioners working in the built environment including architectural photographer Lorenzo Zandri, graphic designers Polytechnic and place futurists The Place Bureau. Join us on 19–20 September when we will open the studios in conjunction with a programme of exhibitions and events by Lorenzo Zandri, Polytechnic, Sammi Gale and The Place Bureau.

name: Boston Manor House
description: Boston Manor House is a Jacobean House built for Lady Mary Reade in 1623 and later owned by the Clitherow family from the 1670s until the 1920s. The House is now open to the public with free entry six days a week. Its beautifully restored historic interiors, including breath-taking ornate plasterwork, are joined by two community exhibition galleries, meeting rooms and an attractive modern café.
address: Boston Manor House, Boston Manor Road, Brentford, TW8 9JX

name: Brentham Garden Suburb
description: Britain's first co-partnership garden suburb, first houses built in 1901. Parker and Unwin's plan introduced in 1907, mainly Arts and Crafts style; fascinating social history.
address: The Brentham Club, 38 Meadvale Road, W5 1NP

name: Brockley's Historic Mews
description: Guided walks through Brockley Conservation Area's quirky mews: leafy lanes, industrial units, Victorian and interesting modern architecture existing in harmony. The cherished public right of way  allows community contact with nature.
address: Wickham Arms, 69 Upper Brockley Road,, SE4 1TF

name: Brockwell Hall
description: Brockwell Hall was originally built in 1811-1813 for a wealthy Ludgate Hill glass maker as the centrepiece of his estate. It has recently been restored by PRS Architects, following an initiative led by Brockwell Hall Community Partners. Original features of the Grade II* listed Recency Villa have been restored and new spaces inside the Hall created for park users and the local community to enjoy.

name: Bruno Court, The German Hospital
description: Modernist extension to Hackney's German Hospital, closed 1987 and converted into flats in 1999.

name: Burgh House
description: Built in 1704 and 1720, Burgh House is a Grade I Listed Queen Anne and early Georgian house situated in the heart of Hampstead Village. As an independent charity, it serves as a cultural hub bringing together heritage, art and community programming. Burgh House is also an Arts Council England accredited museum with a collection relating to Burgh House and the local area.

name: Buzz Bingo Hall (former Granada Cinema)
description: Exceptional example of the luxury cinema 'Picture Palace' of the 1930's with outstanding Gothic interior by Theodore Komisarjevsky and over 3,000-seats. The first and only Grade I listed cinema in the UK.

name: CUFOS - Community Use For the Old Station
description: The former Alexandra Palace Railway Station now run by a small voluntary charity for use by local people and organisations for classes, meetings and many other leisure activities.
address: CUFOS, Top of The Avenue, Muswell Hill, N10 2QE

name: Canal Club
description: The Canal Club, a 1978 modernist community centre designed by Julian Sofaer, is a modest, open-plan space. It features a community garden developed by the boating community moored alongside it.
address: Canal Club Community Garden, Belmont Wharf, Waterloo Gardens, E2 9HP

name: Canons Park
description: Grade II listed historic park landscape containing several listed buildings, including an 18C 'temple' building, bothy and compound, and walled kitchen garden, converted in 1937 to an informally planted garden by Harrow Council.
address: Donnefield Avenue entrance, Canons Park, Edgware, HA8 6RH

name: Caribbean Heritage walking tour of Peckham
description: Gentrification and African Presence in Peckham (GAPP) walking tour highlights the spaces occupied by the Caribbean community, 1960 – 1990. The pinnacle of the walking tour contextualises the significant educational, recreational and cultural spaces which shaped Peckham’s social, cultural, political and economic history over a defined period.
address: Walmer Castle Court, 102 Peckham Road, SE15 2BE

name: Carshalton Water Tower and Historic Gardens
description: Early 18C Grade II listed building incorporating plunge bath with Delft tiles, orangery, saloon and pump chamber with part-restored water wheel. Hermitage and sham bridge in grounds.

name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Islington
description: Visit Islington’s one and only synagogue.  Discover fascinating local Jewish history, an art gallery and much more besides. Learn about Jewish practice, history and culture from the Rabbi - and ask him any questions you like!

name: Chiswick House and Gardens
description: Chiswick House and Gardens is one of the most glorious examples of 18th-century British architecture and landscaped Gardens with over 300 years of discovery, inspiration and delight.
address: Chiswick House and Gardens , Burlington Lane, W4 2RP

name: Christ Church North Finchley, N12 0NU
description: Anglican church building built in 1867 based on the mediaeval Gothic styles of the pre-Reformation era and Gothic revivalist design.

name: Christ Church Southgate and the Minchenden Oak Garden
description: Grade II* listed church with fine collection of Pre-Raphaelite stained glass windows by Morris & Co. including Burne Jones and Rossetti. Wall paintings. Mosaic reredos of the Last Supper by Antonio Salviati. Minchenden Oak  - ancient pollarded oak more than 800 years old.

name: Church of St Lawrence, Little Stanmore
description: Unique Continental Baroque church rebuilt in 1715 by James Brydges, first Duke of Chandos. Painted walls and ceiling with trompe-l'oeil effect. Wood carvings by Grinling Gibbons and the organ on which Handel played.

name: City Information Centre
description: London's main tourist information centre is clad in a specially manufactured system of 220 pre-finished stainless steel panels. The subtly reflective surface provides a striking counterpoint to St Paul's.

name: Clapham Old Town and Venn Street
description: This guided walk around Clapham's Old Town features a radically redesigned public realm which changed the emphasis of the street environment to encourage people to walk and cycle instead of driving.

name: Classical Composers in London
description:
Come and discover the exciting musical world of 18th and 19th Century London when some of Europe's greatest composers and musicians came to stay.

Listen to  stories both successful and tragic of why these great musicians came to London - see where they lived, performed and socialised.

Come and follow in the footsteps of Handel, Haydn, JC Bach, Mozart and Chopin!

name: Cressingham Gardens
description: Low-rise high density estate located next to Brockwell Park. Innovative design with pioneering architectural elements & echoing natural topography. Under threat of demolition by Lambeth council. Tours provided of estate and rotunda.
address: Cressingham Gardens Rotunda, Tulse Hill , SW2 2QG

name: Crown Court Church of Scotland
description: A Church of Scotland in London, home to the longest-established Presbyterian congregation in London, worshipping in this location in Covent Garden since 1719. The current building is red brick with Portland stone dressings in a restrained, finely crafted Free Style. Three storeys, recessed slated attic, mullioned and transomed windows. Fine stained glass, most of which is by Farrar Bell.

name: Croydon Urban Room
description: The Croydon Urban Room is a space to talk about the past, present and future of the Croydon town centre. Through conversa­tions, stories, exhibitions and events, the Urban Room brings together the views of those who live, work and visit the area to create a shared vision of the future and test new uses live in action.

name: Cumberland Road Studios, Wood Green
description:
The Cumberland Road Studios Wood Green is host to about 50 artists and makers currently occupying studios in a 1980s former office building. You will have the opportunity to chat, and see their work and their workspaces as part of their Open Studios weekend.
The building will be active with events including workshops, demonstrations and talks.

name: Deptford Little Farm - Guided Vegetable Tour
description: Deptford Little Farm is a 3,500 sq foot plot with a Dutch style greenhouse growing organic produce and flowers for the Culpeper Family group of pubs. Focusses on permaculture, soil regeneration, organic produce and biodiversity.

name: Dr Johnson's House
description: Fine example of an early 5-floor Queen Anne town house with original panelling, open staircase and unique 'swinging panels' on the open-plan first floor. Johnson compiled his famous 'Dictionary of the English Language' (1755)  here.

name: Drawing Matter
description: Drawing Matter explores the role of drawing in architectural thought and practice. Central to our activities is the Drawing Matter Collection of many thousands of architectural and design drawings from across the world, dating from the Renaissance to the present day.

name: Eastbury Manor House
description: One of the finest surviving Elizabethan red brick Manor houses- Grade I listed. Contains 17th Century wall-paintings, charming walled garden and a fine Tudor tower with original stairs. Many original features have been restored and layout remains mostly unchanged in over 400 years.
address: Eastbury Manor House, Eastbury Square, Barking, IG11 9SN

name: Eastcote Walking Tour
description: Discover the fascinating history of Eastcote and its surroundings, focused on how the landscape has changed, from the exclusively agricultural area to the today's modern suburb, revealing some of the oldest local buildings and their stories
address: Eastcote Station, Field End Road, Pinner, HA5 1QZ

name: Ebbs and flows:  a tour through the evolution of the South Bank
description: A walking tour exploring how movement of people – both daily and generational – has shaped the built environment of the South Bank. From the arrival of the railways to the housing activism of the 1970s and 80s, the tour will look at how the development of new communities has been instrumental in the creation of London’s most vibrant cultural hub
address: Emma Cons Gardens (corner of The Cut and Waterloo Road), SE1 8TQ

name: Emanuel School
description:
Former Royal Patriotic orphanage, converted to school 1883, with 1896 additions and other developments. High Victorian style with stained glass by Moira Forsyth. Set in 12 acres.

In 2022 the building celebrated its 150th anniversary.
address: Battersea Rise (entrance via bridge over the railway on Spencer Park)

name: Epping Forest Visitor Centre at Chingford, The View
description: The Epping Forest Visitor Centre at Chingford is both a visitor centre and museum, it was created from a late 19C stable complex. Enjoy its permanent display about the Forest, temporary exhibitions and unique status as gateway to 6000 acres of Forest trails.

name: Explore the authentically recreated Colony Room
description: A revival and love letter to London’s lost bohemia. Travel back in time to the legendary haunt of some of Soho's greatest creatives.   Featuring pictures, press cuttings and even the piano from the much loved private members club.

name: Exploring the Corbett Estate
description: Join the Archibald Corbett Society for a fascinating two-hour guided walk through Catford's historic Corbett Estate. Led by ACS Secretary Ben Honeybone, you'll explore the estate's late Victorian and early Edwardian history and architecture, including visits to the Grade II listed Corbett Community Library and St Andrew's Church.
address: Brownhill Road Baptist Church, 292 Brownhill Road  Catford, SE6 1AU

name: Feilden Fowles
description: After decades of architecture contributing to environmental damage, a rigorous reset is needed. Feilden Fowles do this through a model that they have developed that is ‘low tech’ in approach. Drop by to meet the team, learn more about their projects and low tech ethos, and to experience their demountable timber studio and their new retrofitted event space, set within a walled garden in Waterloo.

name: Fleet Street Heritage Wall and Sundial
description: The Fleet Street Heritage Wall comprises 86 A3 information panels about the people, places, ideas and newspapers which made the name of Fleet Street famous throughout the world.  From 17th to 20th Sept frequent talks will be given on the sundial and the Heritage Wall, and its innovative design features which will  make it accessible to all comers through web pages, Easy Read pages, and audio files

name: Former Carbonic Gas Works, 142 Lea Bridge Road
description:
Paradise works artist studios in the Old Carbonic Works that is thought to be the birthplace of commercial fizzy drinks in the late 18th Century. It features in the Lea Valley and Hackney Conservation area report found online.


https://hackney.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s68747/240220%20Appendix%20A%20Lea%20Bridge%20Conservation%20Area%20Appraisal.pdf
address: Paradise works, 142 Lea Bridge Road, E5 9RB

name: From Peter Pan to the Time Machine: A Guided Walk
description: How did one small Hampstead street become linked to the discovery of hydrogen, Peter Pan and The Time Machine? What unexpected stories lie behind these elegant facades? This guided walk explores the historic houses, churchyard and streetscape of Church Row and its surroundings, revealing how science, imagination and social change became concentrated in a single corner of London.
address: Outside Hampstead Underground Station (Northern Line), NW3 1QG

name: Fruit to Fashion: how a kitchen garden became a world famous piazza
description:
This year marks the 52nd  anniversary of when the wholesale market ceased trading and moved to the Battersea/Vauxhall area . The tour charts the evolution of Covent Garden, incorporating the piazza, the wholesale produce market, social residential areas and supporting neighbourhoods, and highlighting the social and commercial highs, lows and challenges.
Contact tonyganio@gmail.com

name: Garage Gallery E17
description: In 2022 we created an art gallery in the garage below our house in a residential street in Walthamstow village.   We aim to bring art into our community, acting as a resource to support artists on a not-for-profit basis.  By the time of Open House we will have hosted 26 exhibitions in a wide range of media, by both emerging and more experienced artists.

name: Garrick's Temple to Shakespeare
description: Grade I listed Georgian garden building. Tribute to Shakespeare built in the Ionic style by actor David Garrick. Arcadian Thames-side setting in restored 18C gardens thought to be by Capability Brown.

name: Georgian Clerkenwell's speculative housing boom
description: The early 1800's saw the green fields of northern Clerkenwell spring up into grand squares and terraced houses. This walking tour will look at how the speculative housing developed, what remains today, and the unique stories and characters of the area.
address: Outside Sadler's Wells Theatre, Rosebery Avenue, EC1R 4TN

name: Golders Green Quaker Meeting House
description: Delightful brick and tile building inspired by the famous 1688 Meeting House at Jordans in Buckinghamshire. A simple building in a tranquil setting, reflecting the Quakers' beliefs.

name: Gongoozlers of Regent's Canal & Victoria Park
description: Calling all canal enthusiasts - known as gongoozlers - to walk through the social and industrial history of Victoria Park, Haggerston, and Islington along Regent's Canal. Discover how a purpose-built canal shaped the lives of East Enders, Londoners, and the United Kingdom.
address: Bonner Gate, Sewardstone Road, Bethnal Green, E2 9JW

name: Green Lodge
description: Green Lodge is a low-energy family home by Stylus Architects, carefully embedded into the landscape of Putney Heath. Much of the accommodation is concealed below ground, allowing the building to maintain a modest presence whilst bringing natural light into every room through a series of lightwells and rooflights.

name: Greenside Primary School
description: One of only two primary schools designed by Erno Goldfinger using a pre-cast concrete system - an important modernist building. The building is Grade II* listed and has a fine top-lit mural in the foyer, commissioned by Goldfinger and designed and painted by Gordon Cullen. The 75 year old school needs some serious restoration - come and help us to ensure this gem lives on for future generations

name: Guided Tours and Exhibition at Pioneer Centre, Peckham
description:
Grade II* Listed Modernist building, famously described by Walter Gropius as "an oasis of glass in a desert of brick". Originally built to house 'The Peckham Experiment' an innovative health centre in the 1930s. It was converted to private dwellings in 2000, retaining the indoor pool. 

Join members of our new Community Interest Company set up to mark the centenary and share this unique story.

name: Guided tour of Ladywell and Brockley Cemeteries including the Non-conformist chapel
description:
Starting the Ladywell Cemetery gate,  the tour will take in poets, actors, artists, local dignitaries and war veterans among others.  
The original Non-conformist chapel will be open as well.

name: Guildhall
description: The City's seat of municipal government since 12C. Grade I listed, rare example of medieval civic architecture. Historic banqueting hall and a site of major moments in British history that is still used today.

name: Guildhall Art Gallery
description:
Open daily 10am-5pm. 
Regular free guided tours 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday, with extra tours on the final Open House weekend.
Home of the City of London's art collection, & remains of London's Roman Amphitheatre

name: Guildhall Yard: Meet the Pearly Kings and Queens
description: Publicly accessible space outside the spectacular Grade I listed medieval civic Guildhall.

name: HG Wells' Bromley - in his own words
description: A walk around the streets that the young Herbert George Wells knew when he was growing up and wrote about in his autobiography. You will get a flavour of Bromley in its Victorian heyday - all in the words of the author of the 'Time Machine'

name: Hackney Empire
description: Hackney Empire is a grade II* listed building. The theatre was built as a music hall in 1901, designed by the architect Frank Matcham. It is now a variety theatre for the 21st century, serving the local community and beyond.

name: Hammersmith Quaker Meeting House
description: Recently designated as a Building of Cultural Interest by the Council, the Quaker Meeting House is designed to be a highly sustainable building to embody the Quaker values of simplicity and equality.  The award winning building promotes a sense of calm and tranquility.

name: Hermitage Community Moorings
description: A development of residential and recreational moorings for historic vessels on the Thames. The unique Pier House, built to a high specification, provides a floating community centre just downstream from Tower Bridge.

name: Historic & Modern Buildings in the City
description: On this walk, we will see many historic & modern buildings in the City of London. We’ll look at different architecture styles having regard to the environment and sustainability, from heritage sites to pioneering green tech. Hear about famous architects, past and present, as we explore how the Square Mile preserves its legacy while evolving for a resilient, carbon-neutral tomorrow.

name: Holy Cross Church, Cromer Street
description: Grade ll listed Oxford Movement Anglican church built 1887-88. Historic England describe the exterior as ‘quirky and aggressive’ but the  interior is ‘very spare and elegant'. The building is  interesting for its 2019 conversion of a crypt area, partly rented commercially to a drama school but also used for community groups. On Historic England's Heritage at Risk register with serious cracks.

name: Hopkins Architects
description: The practice's main campus includes two office buildings constructed using its own Patera pre-fabricated system, and linked by a glass reception area and covered walkway.

name: House Mill
description: The World’s largest tidal mill. 5-storey, timber-framed, brick-clad timber watermill with four waterwheels, originally built in 1776 to mill grain for distillery trade. Operational until 1940. On historic 3 Mills Site, Clock Mill adjacent (No access) .
address: Three Mill Lane, Bromley by Bow , E3 3DU

name: Ibraaz
description: Ibraaz is a London-based cultural institution for art, ideas, and dialogue from the Global Majority. Bringing together artists, thinkers, and communities through exhibitions, film, debate, publishing, and multidisciplinary programming, Ibraaz creates a brave space where culture fosters exchange, pluralism, and shared humanity.

name: In Shakespeare's Footsteps
description: In 1949, American actor Sam Wanamaker came looking for Shakespeare in London and could not find much, so decided to re-build the Globe Theatre. Join Lisa who holds a MA in Shakespeare Studies from the Globe Theatre and King's College London and walk in steps of Shakespeare -- and Wanamaker nearly 400 years later.

name: Inner Space Meditation Centre, Covent Garden
description: Inner Space, London’s oasis of calm, welcomes visitors back for the Open House Festival. Join us over two weekends for free Guided Meditations, Personal Development talks and inspiring wellbeing workshops that support and nurture mindfulness, resilience and inner balance. Take a moment to pause in our Quiet Room, a space that will leave you feeling reconnected, refreshed, uplifted, and renewed.

name: Isokon Building (Lawn Road Flats)
description: Grade I listed 1934 residential block of flats in Hampstead, designed by the Canadian modernist architect Wells Coates for clients Jack and Molly Pritchard. English Heritage blue plaque for Bauhaus masters Gropius, Breuer and Moholy-Nagy. Museum on site.

name: Jacksons Lane Arts Centre
description: Jacksons Lane’s year-round programme of contemporary performance, arts participation and cultural education exists to empower, and ignite creativity within diverse communities & work tirelessly to overcome traditional barriers through art.

name: Jubilee Hall Parsonage Lane
description: A rare example of a once ubiquitous structure - the military hut. This one probably dates from World War I; it was later sold off and moved to its present site, where it was in turn a Boys Brigade HQ, a book store and, from 1986, the home of the Enfield Society.

name: Kaymet Factory
description: The operational factory of Kaymet, a maker of trays and trolleys since 1947. A hidden 1950s building with a small yard, originally a printing works. It is brick built, with clear-storey glazing and tubular truss north-light main shed roof.

name: Kenwood
description: A striking Neoclassical villa in tranquil gardens on Hampstead Heath, Kenwood boasts breath-taking interiors by Robert Adam and a world-class art collection.

name: Kingsland Basin Moorings (CHUG)
description: Small is beautiful: 6ft narrowboats provide individual design solutions for living and working in confined conditions. The self-managed moorings are a unique community with shared open spaces, offering a glimpse of alternative urban living. There's a floating allotment too!

name: Kingswood House
description: Grade II listed building owned by Southwark Council. Large, 19th century mansion built in the form of a stone-faced baronial castle for the inventor of Bovril. Interior includes substantial wood panelling and a great hall. The building is managed by HH KIngswood Ltd and is used as a cultural and community space.

name: Lansbury Lawrence Primary School
description: Lansbury Lawrence (formally Susan Lawrence and Elizabeth Lansbury) opened in the 1951 Festival of Britain as a showpiece of the Live Architecture exhibition in the Lansbury Estate. An interesting mid-century design with original features.

name: Lauderdale House
description: Grade II* listed building in Waterlow Park dating to 1582. Original Tudor wooden framework adapted by successive owners over the centuries. Today the House runs primarily as an arts, heritage and education centre.

name: Leadenhall Market
description: Iconic Victorian covered market, with roots in Roman Londinium. Today, more than 40 renowned retail brands and outstanding food and drink venues are set within the stunning market place.

name: Leafy Southgate: N14 landscape and suburbia
description: A walking tour exploring the development of Southgate from the 18th century to the present day. From landed estates to interwar suburbia and beyond, this walk will uncover masterpieces of Modernist architecture, compare the municipal and suburban influences on the area, and challenge preconceived notions of ‘natural’ landscapes.

name: London Open Form Pavilion of Air
description: A floating acoustic architecture, playfully reframing public space as an essential community engagement through sound & site mapping. Accessed by smartphone, headphones & echoes.xyz app, the Pavilion is located outside the Serpentine Gallery,. Drawing on Oskar & Zofia Hansen’s Open Form architectural concept it is one of 15 in a series including Venice, Berlin, Dublin, Bergen and Arctic Norway.

name: London's Roman Amphitheatre
description: The capital’s only Roman Amphitheatre. Regular combined guided tours of Amphitheatre and Guildhall Art Gallery at 12.15pm & 1.15pm on Tuesday-Sunday. Additional Open House tours on 19 and 20 September, please see Guildhall Art Gallery listing.
address: London’s Roman Amphitheatre at Guildhall Art Gallery, Guildhall Yard

name: Lorenzo Zandri - Urban Narrative
description: During the festival, Lorenzo Zandri’s studio transforms into an immersive environment that bridges the gap between architectural theory and photographic practice. Eschewing traditional construction to focus on the 'process of the image’, Zandri will present an analytical overview of his practice and research – where photography serves as a tool for urban narrative rather than mere documentation.
address: Bodney Road Studios, 1 Bodney Road, Unit 2, E8 1AY

name: Marie's Wardrobe
description: This renovation reworks a 20th-century London townhouse with a perforated plywood stair and extensive timber interventions that introduce light, structure, and continuity. Texts engraved into the stair and screen record the collaborative design dialogue. A cantilevered balcony connects the kitchen and garden with minimal structure and visual weight.

name: Methodist Central Hall Westminster
description: A masterpiece of Edwardian neo-baroque architecture opposite Westminster Abbey.  Second largest self-supporting ferro-concrete dome in world. Its Great Hall was the venue for the Inaugural General Assembly of the United Nations in 1946.

name: Monoux Almshouses
description: A row of thirteen dwellings plus a hall used as a committee room and offices, constructed as one block on two floors. The building is divided by a jettied cross range. Grade II listed.

name: Morris+Company | 'Waste Not: Materials, Making and the Circular Economy' Exhibition
description: Morris+Company is an award-winning architecture practice based in Hackney, east London. We have applied circular economy principles to the retrofit of our own studio, gallery and café space on Mare Street, reducing waste, reusing materials, and designing for longevity.  We place the creative ‘act’ of architecture onto the high street, reveal our practice to the public and engage local communities.

name: Museum of London Docklands
description: Grade I listed, late Georgian sugar warehouse now housing the Museum of London Docklands. Sensitively restored, the new multimedia displays coexist with the massive timber and brick structures of the original building.
address: No. 1 Warehouse, West India Quay (off Hertsmere Road), E14 4AL

name: National Youth Theatre
description:
Public Tours tours by Architect's DSDHA and the NYT team of the recently redeveloped RIBA-award-winning building, and a first look at materials from the National Youth Theatre archive, made public for the first time as part of their 70th anniversary celebrations. 

This project is supported by the Mayor of London and the National Lottery Heritage Fund.
address: National Youth Theatre, 443-445 Holloway Road, N7 6LW

name: Never mind the bollards, here's the walking tour
description: This walking tour tells the story of central London though one of it’s most abundant and unnoticed elements of street furniture – the humble bollard. Standing proud on our pavements, these posts carry peculiar stories, protect buildings of historic significance, and come in an array of beautiful shapes and sizes. Come along to learn more about our streets’ cast iron compatriots.

name: North London Collegiate School - Canons House
description: North London Collegiate School, founded in 1850, is a leading independent day school for girls aged 4-18. Located at the historic Canons House, a Grade II listed building from the 18th century, the school offers a stimulating environment where bright young minds can explore, question, and thrive academically. The school resides in an important historic site, surrounded by Canons Park since 1929.

name: Ongéan
description:
Ongéan Ecosystem : 
Art Studios, Gallery, Performance Space, Edible Garden & Kitchen. All built and designed with 99% Reclaimed Materials by artist Adam Ge-Saelis.
address: Ongéan, Park Mews, Croxted rd, SE24 9DB

name: Our Yard at Clitterhouse Farm
description: Come and visit this grassroots community enterprise where old meets new in the form of the historic farm buildings alongside our crowdfunded cafe. Find out how some of these historic buildings have been saved and lovingly bought back into community use, and find out about our future plans.
address: Clitterhouse Playing Fields, Claremont Rd, NW2 1AP

name: Paekakariki Press
description: Paekakariki Press Ltd is a letterpress workshop containing equipment that can support the letterpress printing processes from casting type to binding a finished book printed on our Heidelberg Cylinder

name: Parish Church of St Mary The Virgin Lewisham
description:
The church was rebuilt in late 15th century with some of that still remaining to this day.							
During the festival there will be opportunity to self-guide or join a group tour which will include access to restricted areas such as the crypt and tower. These last about 30 min and will start on each hour with the last starting at 3 pm

name: Paxton Locher House
description: A unique modern courtyard house making brilliant use of an off-street site on Clerkenwell Green. A retractable glass roof gives wonderful natural light all year round and opens the house to the sky in dry weather.

name: Phoenix Cinema
description: One of the oldest cinemas in the country with a barrel-vaulted ceiling and Art Deco wall reliefs by Mollo and Egan. Grade II listed.

name: Phoenix Gardens Community Building
description: The first purpose-built new-build community centre to be built in the heart of Soho for generations, located within the renowned Phoenix Gardens. Winner: RIBA London Award. Designed by RIBA London Architect of the Year Winner.

name: Quaker Meeting House, Wanstead
description: A Modernist building of four hexagons within an Epping Forest setting. A sunny meeting room for Quaker worship faces a wooded burial ground of simple headstones, including those of Elizabeth Fry, William Mead, Guilielma Lister and Norman Frith.

name: Queen Elizabeth's Hunting Lodge
description: Grade II* Tudor timber-framed hunt standing/grandstand (1543) with Henry VIII Tudor food display. Gateway to 6,000 acres of ancient Epping Forest, once a royal hunting ground, protected since 1878 by the City of London.

name: Queer Britain
description: Queer Britain Museum is the UK’s national LGBTQ+ museum.    Housed in a converted Victorian building in the heart of the regenerated King’s Cross area, the galleries feature over 200 objects from over 100 years of queer history.   At Open House 2026, Queer Britain’s volunteer guides will give talks demonstrating the museum’s mission to reclaim, preserve and inspire LGBTQ+ history.

name: RC Church of St Mellitus
description: A grand neo-classical building of 1871 with impressive interior, built as New Court Congregational Chapel. Home to a Hunter pipe organ, installed as a WW1 memorial and recently restored with National Lottery Heritage Fund support.
address: St Mellitus RC Church, Tollington Park, N4 3AG

name: Rachwalsky House
description:
Grade II Modernist House designed by German emigre architect Rudolf Frankel for his sister and family in 1938. The house remains remarkably intact and retains the layout and original features which adhere to Modernist principles of the era.

Guided tours at 10:00, 12:00, 14:00 and 16:00.

name: Regent Street Cinema (The University of Westminster)
description: The University of Westminster was one of the first polytechnics in the UK – established in 1838, to educate the working people of London, regardless of background and financial status. Housed in the building is the Regent Street Cinema, widely regarded as the ‘birthplace of British cinema’, with the first public premiere of film in the UK by the Lumière Brothers using the Cinématographe in 1896.

name: Regent's Park Estate Story Trail  Guided Tour
description:
Launched on 24th April 2025, Regent’s Park Estate Story Trail is an exciting new resident-led socially engaged public art trail through Regent’s Park Estate, Euston. 

The trail encompasses 12 site-specific art installations created by 10 artists and collectives, bringing 31 new public artworks to Regent's Park Estate.
address: Old Diorama Arts Centre, 201 Drummond Street, NW1 3FE

name: Richmond Lock Building (Surrey Side)
description:
A good example of quality late-Victorian functional design.
Richmond Lock &Weir consists of three 32 ton weir gates that operate 2 hours either side of high water.

name: Roe Green Village
description: Built in 1918-19 as a 'Munitions Village' to provide housing for AirCo (the Aircraft Manufacturing Company based in Colindale), Roe Green was designed in the garden village idiom by Sir Frank Baines, who was one of HM Office of Works principal architects and a former pupil of C. R. Ashbee. Its picturesque Arts & Crafts character echoes that of Baines's earlier Well Hall Estate (1915) in Eltham.

name: Romanian Cultural Institute
description: Situated in one of the largest and grandest 19th century squares in London, 1 Belgrave Square was acquired by Romania in 1936 and is now home to the Romanian Cultural Institute.

name: Royal Foundation of St Katharine
description: Founded by Queen Matilda in 1147 and with HM Queen Elizabeth II as our previous patron, The Royal Foundation of St Katharine has served as a centre for worship, hospitality and service over many centuries. With 45 bedrooms, 11 meeting rooms, and a community café, it is a unique, quiet sanctuary in the heart of London.

name: Royalty Studios - Building Tours by Architect
description: Mike McMahon Studio has redesigned a 1980s postmodern office building in Notting Hill, adding new CLT storeys topped with a fluted brick crown. The project retains the original brick structure while using lightweight timber construction to reduce embodied carbon and minimise intervention. New interiors and gardens complete the scheme.

name: Sadler's Wells East
description: Tours of the Sadler's Wells theatre on Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park - Sadler's Wells East.

name: Sands End Arts & Community Centre
description: Amongst the RIBA Stirling Prize shortlist 2022 sits Mæ Architect's Sands End Arts & Community Centre in Fulham. The centre consists of a single-storey building comprising bright, airy and flexible event spaces and a community café.

name: Seven Acre Lake, Canons Park Estate
description: Private 18C Seven Acre Lake, part of the dismantled Canons Mansion grounds, now surrounded by 1930s character housing. Wildlife includes Canada geese, swans and ducks.
address: Rose Garden Close, off Canons Drive, Edgware, HA8 7RF

name: Shaftesbury Hall
description:
Shaftesbury Hall is a Tin Tabernacle  rebuilt by North London Samaritans in 2018 to replicate the original Hall built in the 1890s.
It has been owned by North London Samaritans for 50 years and since the rebuild is used as a Community Hub, with our branch of Samaritans at the rear.

name: Shrewsbury House
description: Built in 1923, to replace its 18C namesake, Grade ll listed Shrewsbury House is the focus of the Shrewsbury Park Estate conservation area, built 1934-1936 by John Laing and Sons. Two 20th Century Civil Defence buildings are situated within the grounds as well as listed garden features including a recently restored summer house.

name: Soho - forever changing
description: The area post 1700 became very cosmopolitan with immigrants mainly from Europe, and their influence on food and drink became increasingly important. This tour is based on food and drink, passing by restaurants, pubs, coffee bars,  pâtisserie and  delis that have been present for decades, finishing at a relatively new site.
address: Opposite Coach and Horses , Greek street/ Romilly Street, W1D 5DH

name: South Ealing Cemetery Chapels
description:
Designed by local architect Charles Jones in 1861, the chapels are constructed of ragstone with limestone dressings in a Gothic style.   
There is a central porte cochere (archway for carriages) with clock and belfry, flanked by the South and North Chapels. These are set in a large area of naturalised woodland with interesting and atmospheric memorials and benches for peaceful, relaxation

name: South London Theatre
description: Grade II listed 1881 former fire station with prominent watch tower and original fire doors.
address: The Old Fire Station, 2a Norwood High Street, SE27 9NS

name: Southbank Printmakers
description:
We are a friendly artist run gallery in Wells Street offering affordable, handmade fine art prints with a broad range of subjects created using many different printmaking techniques.
We aim to encourage people who have never encountered art before to experience printmaking through our regular workshops.

name: Southlands Arts Centre
description: Explore Southlands Arts Centre and discover the history and architecture of this Grade II listed Queen Anne-style building. Admire its distinctive red-brick façade, elegant decorative detailing and historic interiors, and learn how this former private residence has evolved into a thriving community arts centre, celebrating Hillingdon's rich architectural and cultural heritage.
address: Southlands Arts Centre, 75, The Green, West Drayton, UB7 7PW

name: St Andrew's Kingsbury (new church)
description: Meticulous 1930s rebuilding (complete with original furnishings) of an 1840s Marylebone church. Grade I listed. Contains works by Pugin, Burges, Street, Pearson and Butterfield.
address: Junction of Church Lane/Tudor Gardens/ Old Church Lane, Kingsbury

name: St Augustine's Church
description: St. Augustine's, Kilburn affectionately known as 'The Cathedral of North London' was established in 1870. Fr. Kirkpatrick, the first Vicar, engaged John Loughborough Pearson as the architect with the result being what many consider one of his finest works. Externally in 1890 with the tower and spire it became the 2nd tallest building in London (now ecclesiastically 2nd to St. Paul's Cathedral).

name: St Bartholomew's Hospital
description: The Grade I listed North Wing at St Bartholomew’s Hospital in the City of London houses two of England’s most important interiors, the Great Hall, and the Hogarth Stair with its large paintings by William Hogarth. The hospital was designed by architect James Gibbs and construction of the North Wing was completed in 1732.
address: St Bartholomew's Hospital, West Smithfield, EC1A 7BE

name: St Bride's Church, Fleet Street
description: Wren designed building of 1675, interior lost in blitz of 1940, reopened 1957 with 'Wren inspired' interior
address: St Bride's Church, St Bride's Avenue, EC4Y 8AU

name: St George's Cathedral
description: A stunning cathedral in the heart of London. Discover the story of a forgotten masterpiece. Designed by Augustus Pugin and opened in 1848, the original cathedral was hailed as England's foremost Catholic church before an incendiary bomb devastated the building in 1941. Explore the history, architecture and legacy that shaped the Cathedral you see today—and discover its remarkable story.

name: St James's Piccadilly
description: St James's Piccadilly is a Grade I listed Christopher Wren church in the heart of the West End. Completed in 1684, and known as the Artists' Church, its interiors include historic works of art by Grinling Gibbons (reredos, organ case and font), postwar Classical interiors by Albert Richardson, and contemporary art by Che Lovelace honouring the 18th-century abolitionist Quobna Ottobah Cugoano.

name: St John at Hackney
description: St John at Hackney Church has been Hackney's centre of Christian worship since 1275. The current church was completed in 1792, with major restoration finished in 2020. It's a major ringing centre in East London with ten bells from 4 to 16 cwt - eight from 1957 following the 1955 fire, and two added in 2004. This very active tower rings for Sunday services, national celebrations and commemorations.
address: St John at Hackney Church, Lower Clapton Road, E5 0PD

name: St Lawrence Jewry
description:
First built in c.1136, St. Lawrence Jewry was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666. The present church was designed by Sir Christopher Wren in 1671. The interiors were destroyed in December 1940 during the World War Two and restored in 1957, faithful to Wren’s original design. Extensive conservation works were completed in 2023.
The official church to the City of London Corporation.

name: St Mark's Church, Biggin Hill
description:
The Moving Church.
On his appointment to Biggin Hill in 1951, Rev Vivian Symons had the vision to bring the materials for a new church building from the disused All Saints, North Peckham. But first, he had to deconstruct a huge Victorian church, and bring it by himself to its new site.
However, St Mark's is Grade 2 listed, not because of its origin, but due to its style.
address: St Mark's Church, 10 Church Road, Biggin Hill, TN16 3LB

name: St Mark’s Church
description: A Grade 2-listed mid-Victorian parish church in the Gothic style,  built of Kentish ragstone with a slate roof.  Unique features include a panel of hand-made decorated tiles beyond the High Altar - probably Royal Doulton - and five noted stained glass windows, probably by Alfred Hemming.  The baptistery is also noteworthy, with its font and five murals of Biblical scenes, painted in oil on canvas.

name: St Mary & St Joseph Roman Catholic Church, Poplar
description: Grade II Listed.   Designed by Adrian Gilbert Scott.  Cruciform shape (120 feet by 120 feet) of steel girder and brick construction. Its Lantern tower – based on Ely Cathedral – is supported on parabolic arches 35 feet wide and 50 feet high.  The Stained Glass Windows were designed by John Wilson of Edinburgh and the Stations of the Cross  carved in Blue Horton Stone by Peter Watts.
address: St Mary & St Joseph Church, Upper North Street, Poplar, London

name: St Mary's Church, Battersea
description: During Open House, the Friends of Battersea Parish Church present a Floral Festival, organ recitals, historical displays, alongside 3 talks exploring history, creativity, sanctuary & Battersea’s radical past. Sat 12 Sept Dr. Peter Rumley at 6pm, Tues 15 Guy Stagg at 6.30pm,  Thurs 17 at 6.30pm Rory Walsh & Mike Squires.  Plus Join us for Choral Evensong amidst the flowers at St Mary’s Battersea.

name: St Matthias Old Church - Community Centre
description: Oldest building in Docklands built in the Gothic and Classical styles, with original 17C stonework and fine mosaics. One of only three churches built during the Civil War, it was originally the East India Company Chapel.

name: St Michael and All Angels Church
description: James Maltby Bignall (1827-1885) worked in the practice of Sir George Gilbert Scott, the architect of St Pancras Station. The style of St Michael's is late Gothic Revival, in its size and height reminiscent of Northern European churches.

name: St Michael's Chester Square
description: St Michael's Chester Square is a grade 2 listed church in the heart of Victoria, built in the late Decorated Gothic style. The War Memorial Chapel at the north east end of the church was designed by Giles Gilbert Scott and completed in 1920. The stained glass West Window is by Hugh Easton and two windows to the south are by Morris & Co and date to 1882.

name: St Olave Hart Street
description: A Great Fire Survivor, damaged in the blitz, the post war restoration of this fascinating building began 75 years ago this year.  Described by John Betjeman as a 'country church in the world of Seething Lane' the building uniquely blends medieval fabric with Festival of Britain era motifs. Explore the medieval crypt, 'Pepys' vestry, church tower and ringing room. Bellringing demonstrations.

name: St Paul's Bow Common
description: Described as 'the most significant church built after the WWII in Britain' - Brutalist, inclusive and influential signpost for future church design.
address: Corner of Burdett Road/ St Paul's Way, E3 4AR

name: St Paul's Church, Winchmore Hill
description: Church of England parish church built in 1826-27 by John Davies. It is one of the early Commissioners' churches built after the Battle of Waterloo. It forms part of the Winchmore Hill Conservation Area. The chancel was added in 1888-89, and further extended for the church's centenary in 1928. The church is open daily, and there will be guided tours and a special exhibition 19-20 September.
address: St Paul's Church, Church Hill, N21 1JA

name: St Paul's, Newington
description: Modern architecture church with large copper and lead roof and concrete, brick and stained glass external structure. Marble, wood and plaster interior and artwork by Sculptor Freda Pinto and Gerald Holtom.

name: St Peter's Church Petersham
description: St Peter's Church has Saxon origins. It was rebuilt in the 11th century and enlarged in 1505. Norman, Tudor and Georgian features can be viewed. The church has a small nave but large and unequal-sized transepts. It is best known for its Georgian box pews. The two-decker (originally three-) pulpit dates from 1796. The churchyard contains several memorials of historical and architectural interest.
address: Church Lane, off The Petersham Road, Richmond, TW10 7AB

name: St. George Villa
description:
Tranquility in an urban environment, this project has transformed an unloved basement into a light filled, sustainable, calming home.

A deep retrofit using low-carbon materials, including a high level of insulation, a natural swimming pool, rainwater harvesting and a green roof, this home explores how we can transform high density urban areas into places of harmony between people and nature.

name: St. Mary's Church, Walthamstow Village
description: Grade II* listed church dating from 12C with Medieval, Tudor, Georgian & Victorian features. 16C Tower. Church refurbishment and new extension completed in 2023. Over 1300 monuments with four Grade II listed tombs in churchyard.
address: Church End (top of Church Hill), Walthamstow, E17 9RJ

name: St. Stephen's Hounslow Conservation Area - Open Gardens
description: The community of St. Stephen's Hounslow Conservation Area opens private gardens in celebration of our trees. St. Stephen's Road is defined by the century-old lime trees. Yet, all of the trees within the conservation area are protected, not just those along the road. Join us to visit a variety of public and private gardens, celebrating the rich history and biodiversity of our conservation area.
address: St. Stephens Church, Parkside Road, Hounslow, TW3 2BP

name: Stanley Arts
description:
First opened in 1903, Stanley Arts continues its building's legacy as a beacon for the local community. This Grade II listed Edwardian theatre, gallery, and public hall reflects its founder's interest in the arts and sciences.

The historic features of the building are sometimes hidden, other times flaunted. Our Open House tours cover everything past and present about this storied institution.

name: Stationers' Hall
description: 17C livery hall with courtroom and garden. Oak panelling and stained glass windows. Undamaged in WWII. Recently refurbished new rooms and air-cooling within, including a new lift for step-free access into the Hall. Selected items from the archives on display. Book binding exhibition in the Hall.

name: String House - Camberwell
description: Contemporary timber frame home with unique string screen; a postwar house reassembled to follow passive house principles. The structure was built in 7 weeks to create a reimagined flexible home of two halves enabling an Airbnb rental that bypasses the first floor kitchen & living area, located to borrow views towards mature trees at the rear & city buses to the front expanding senses & spaces.

name: Swakeleys Estate
description: A most important house in Ickenham, an outstanding example of Jacobean architecture built in the 1630s. Red brick construction laid in English bond on an H plan. Great Hall includes the 1655 Harrington Screen, 18C marble fireplace panelling.
address: Swakeleys Road, Ickenham (access from Milton Road), UB10 8LD

name: TOMA House + Studio
description: A self-built project by the founder of east London architecture practice TOMA Studio, this mid-terraced Victorian house has been completely re-imagined over the course of three years. The house balances refined detailing with experimentation to create a spacious and comfortable family home, which also accommodates an architecture practice and pottery studio within a Shou Sugi Ban garden room.

name: Temple Bar
description: Temple Bar is a 350 year old gateway to the City of London, designed by Sir Christopher Wren. It formerly stood in Fleet Street, and is the last surviving gateway to the City of London. This beautiful structure has a fascinating history, which will be revealed to visitors.
address: First Floor, Paternoster Lodge, 2 Paternoster Square, EC4M 7DX

name: The Annual Sedici Post Grad Group Exhibition
description:
Now in its seventeenth year, Sedici consists of artists from many countries who are now based across England. Working across eclectic mediums and subject matter, this diverse body of artists share an independent and contemporary purpose highlighting the ongoing strength of Art being made today. 

The gallery itself is a reimagined, mid-century school gymnasium with original details

name: The Barbican & The City Gardens
description: The Barbican is a residential complex of around 2,000 flats, maisonettes, and houses in the City of London. Built on the site destroyed by The Blitz during the World War II, The Barbican Estate is a fascinating development and an icon of Brutalist architecture. Architects were Chamberlain, Powell and Bon. You will find an oasis in the middle of buildings, with gardens and water features.

name: The Battle of Britain Bunker - The Generator House
description: Explore the Generator House at RAF Uxbridge’s Battle of Britain Bunker. Normally off‑limits to the public, it houses the original 1930s standby generator that powered the underground Operations Room coordinating RAF Fighter Command in WWII. It offers a glimpse into wartime engineering, featuring preserved machinery, original fittings, and fascinating stories.  Free admission, no booking required.

name: The British Academy
description: One of London's finest examples of Georgian architecture, Carlton House Terrace is a Grade I listed structure originally designed by John Nash and built between 1827 and 1833. Today the townhouse is home to the British Academy, the UK’s national academy for the humanities and social sciences, and boasts an impressive art collection, including works by David Hockney and Wilhelmina Barns-Graham.

name: The Brunel Museum
description: London's story of an engineering family that changed the world. Dramatic new staircase below sculpture garden leads to underground chamber. Travel by train through first underwater shopping arcade & fairground to view Thames Tunnel portico.

name: The Butcher, The Baker and The Candlestick Maker
description: Trade and craft guilds have flourished for centuries. The City of London’s Livery Companies are unique in their survival, number, and diversity. While the original social and economic conditions that created these original guilds have long been overtaken by modern commerce, these fascinating institutions still flourish today. Join us to explore their enduring history and modern impact.

name: The Great Barn, Harmondsworth
description: This year we’re celebrating the 600th anniversary of Harmondsworth’s magnificent Great Barn. It’s over 190 feet long, nearly 40 feet high, and over 95% of its structural timbers are original. Displays include details of its construction, the conservation/repairs carried out in 2014, and its place in the agricultural history of the village.
address: Manor Court, High Street, Harmondsworth, UB7 0AQ

name: The Great Fire of London
description:
On Sunday, 2 September 1666, the Great Fire of London started at a bakery in Pudding Lane, destroying thousands of homes, 87 churches, and St. Paul's Cathedral.
On this walk, we will explore this dramatic story, discover the causes and outcomes of the fire and see how Christopher Wren helped rebuild the city from the ashes.

name: The Lock House, Richmond Lock & Weir
description: The Lock House is part of Richmond Lock & Weir, on the left bank of the Thames at Richmond. Originally home to the resident lock keeper, it is now the design studio and exhibition space of Astronaut Kawada, architects and designers. They have fully refurbished the interior of the Lock House to create a series of spaces to complement the remarkable and unique qualities of the main structure.
address: The Lock House, Ranelagh Drive, TW1 1QZ

name: The Making of Pimlico
description: A walking tour exploring  the work of early 19th century master-builder, Thomas Cubitt. Explores how the area has changed and been shaped by some of the important and influential planning, housing and design ideas of its time.
address: Pimlico Tube station, Rampayne Street, SW1V 2JA

name: The Old Church Stoke Newington
description: The Old Church 1563 is a not for profit arts and music venue, in the heart of Stoke Newington and the only surviving Elizabethan church in London. Built on the site of a church that dates back to the Doomsday Book our enclosed graveyard contains monuments to people who were prominent in the fight against the slave trade and Anna Barbauld, poet and proto-feminist.

name: The Old Fire Station
description: The Old Fire Station is now a thriving community centre run by the Holloway Neighbourhood Group. It has been redeveloped for this purpose, now housing a community room, garden room and hall. The building has many original features (notably on the outside) and even though the usage has changed dramatically it remains an important emergency service for many in the local area.

name: The Old Schoolhouse
description: Originally St, Mary's Infants School, later as Holy Innocents' National School until 1934. It then became derelict until 1981 when, after refurbishment, it became headquarters of the Hornsey Historical Society.

name: The Ragged School SE1
description: Built in 1907, The Ragged School SE1 has been part of the community for nearly 120 years.  starting off as a poor school in the worst and first borough of London, the school aimed to transform lives of the ragged children that lined the streets.  The church then took over the school to form a club,  pass through developers into the hands of an artist.  The White room will open for creative delight.
address: The Ragged School, 47 Union Street, SE1 1SG

name: The Royal Society
description: A spectacular Grade I listed building designed by famed architect John Nash. Built in 1831, these former townhouses have undergone refurbishments throughout their history. The building is now home to the UK's national science academy.
address: The Royal Society, 6-9 Carlton House Terrace, SW1Y 5AG

name: Thornhill Square
description: A tour of one of the largest and best preserved early Victorian squares and gardens in London, also with a magnificent and original public library of 1906, which shows Byzantine and Art Nouveau influences, and a remarkable Gothic church. Refreshments available.
address: Main door of St Andrew’s Church, Bridgeman Road, N1 1BQ

name: Tower Gardens Garden Suburb
description: One of the first garden suburbs in the world, 2-storey terraced cottages retaining decorative architectural features. LCC created 'housing of the working classes' role for architects' department under Riley, member of the Art Workers guild.
address: 5 Tower Gardens Road, North Tottenham, N17 7PX

name: Triangle House
description: Winner of the 2025 Camden Design Award for small projects and the 2024 'Don't Move Improve' award for best project under £100k. A self build 39m2 triangular micro home converted from a former mechanic's garage,  creating a flexible and multifunctional home fit for living and working in.  Come and see sliding beds, triangular sofas and a pocket garden.

name: Trinity Buoy Wharf/Container City
description:
Home to London's only lighthouse, fine stock buildings, examples of the innovative Container City buildings and SS Robin, the world’s only surviving complete
Victorian steamship. This former buoy manufacturing site is now a centre for the creative industries with various sculptures and installations.

name: Trinity Laban Conservatoire of Music and Dance
description:
Part of Trinity Laban's multi-borough campus, the Laban Building is the largest purpose-built contemporary dance centre in the world. 

A gently curving facade with richly coloured plastic-cladding leads into spaces filled with vivid colour and dynamic form.

name: Two Temple Place
description: Completed in 1895, Two Temple Place is a dazzling neo-Gothic gem on the Victoria Embankment, designed by gothic revivalist architect, John Loughborough Pearson, & commissioned by & built for William Waldorf Astor, as his estate office.

name: WWII fighter pen tours at former RAF Kenley
description: Join us for an open tour exploring the architecture, use, and restoration of the WWII fighter pens and air raid shelters that were part of RAF Kenley's airfield defenses.

name: Walking tour of Chiswick House Gardens
description: Walking tour of Chiswick house Gardens
address: Meet in front of Chiswick House, W4 2RP

name: Walthamstow Pumphouse Museum
description: Grade II listed Victorian engine house remodelled to take a pair of 1895 Marshall steam engines, still in working order. A museum celebrating the rich Industrial Heritage of the Borough and the Lea Valley Region.

name: Walthamstow Wetlands
description:
Discover a piece of London’s industrial past, surrounded by nature.
Join us at the wetlands for a special tour of the Victorian Engine House, once a pumping station and now a welcoming visitor centre. Climb the steps of the old Coppermill Tower, first mentioned in the Domesday Book, and enjoy great views from the top.
address: Marine Engine House, 2 Forest Road, N17 9NH

name: Wanstead Heritage Walk
description: A guided walk, Wanstead Station to The Temple, Wanstead Park, taking in Wanstead's history and architectural heritage. The walk finishes at The Temple and will include an optional private tour of its displays.

name: Wapping Hydraulic Power Station
description: rare opportunity to see inside Wapping Hydraulic Power Station, built in 1890 and London's last hydraulic power station to be decommissioned. The site has been closed for the last ten years, but is now entering a new era under the custodianship of Glass Castle Foundation, which has begun restoration ahead of plans to breathe new life into the building as a  centre for experimental arts.
address: Wapping Hydraulic Power Station, Wapping Wall, E1W 3SF

name: William Mitchell's Mural at Brooklands Primary School
description: Join us at Brooklands Primary School to discover more about the story of William Mitchell’s mural (1958), designed as part of the London County Council’s pioneering Design Consultant Scheme
address: Brooklands Primary School, Medbourne Close, SE3 9AB

name: Wimbledon Windmill Museum
description: Rare example of a hollow post mill (1817). Grade II* listed, it now contains a museum depicting the history and development of windmills in Britain. Many working models, windmill machinery, equipment and tools.

name: Wolves Lane Horticultural Centre
description: Ever explored an eco-building? Wolves Lane Horticulture centre is home to a thriving 3.5 acre contemporary community food growing space alongside 1970s glasshouses. Visit the cactus and palm house with koi carp alongside a “bale” of terrapins and exotic flora and fauna. The café serves healthy, locally grown produce and the shop will furnish you with plants to take home.
address: Wolves Lane Centre, Wolves Lane, N22 5JD

name: Woolwich Works
description: Welcome to Woolwich Works - a multi-disciplinary cultural hub on the Royal Arsenal in Woolwich. Originally used in the manufacturing of armaments and ammunition, these five listed buildings now house cutting-edge contemporary music, award-winning stand-up comedy, as well as theatre, dance, cabaret and everything in between.
address: The Fireworks Factory, 11 No. 1 Street, SE18 6HD

name: York House
description: Mid-17C house, a scheduled ancient monument, with fine staircase and 18C additions.

name: outhouse gallery
description:
outhouse gallery is a small, independent, artist-run creative space located in Brunswick Park, Camberwell. 
As a former public toilet, the gallery's mission is to be open, public and accessible to both facilitators and visitors - from free exhibitions, live performances, and workshops to publishing articles online and in outhouse magazine.
